finding.reason: The standard-fs release reads/parses the lock, verifies token+pid, then unlinks the path. That is not an atomic ownership check: a foreign replacement after readback and before unlink is deleted. The implementation itself labels this best-effort; the exact-ownership invariant is therefore not preserved.
deterministic_injected_fs_trace: Initialize files[lockPath] with token A and pid A; hold A release handle.
readFileSync(lockPath) snapshots and returns token-A bytes, but before returning replaces files[lockPath] with token B/pid B.
release parses the returned A bytes and passes the token/pid check.
unlinkSync(lockPath) deletes the current path entry, token B; release returns true.
finding.fixture_gap: dashboard-regression.fixture.mjs:2056-2061 installs token B before calling release, so readback observes B and safely returns false. It does not replace the file between readFileSync and unlinkSync. The same-token and repeat-acquire cases are also sequential.
finding.root_recovery: Inspected stale-lock handling returns STALE_LOCK_ROOT_RECOVERY_REQUIRED; automatic Root cleanup and serialization with release are comments, not an enforced or independently proven mechanism in the reviewed source/fixture.
finding.required_fix: Do not use pathname read-then-unlink as exact release. Use a genuinely atomic ownership-aware relinquish primitive, or keep shared-lock cleanup in serialized Root recovery after the old owner is stopped. Add the injected interleaving above and assert token B remains untouched.
